note: XXVII: Mina at the rock above the bridge (Google, Cole bridge as reference; Ian on his phone)
style: An oil painting in colour of 1893 matching the first reference image: the same great ancient stone bridge with carved gargoyles over a deep snowy gorge, the same ruined castle on its crag, the same blood-red sunset sky, in the manner of Thomas Cole: grand landscape, dramatic architecture, strong value contrast, loose visible brushwork. No text, signature or border.

beats.text: Shot: wide, from behind. Behind a great snow-covered rock high on the slope above the bridgehead, looking down over the shoulders of a young woman in a dark hooded cloak holding a revolver and an elderly grey-haired man crouching beside her, onto the great stone bridge just below them where riders in sheepskins and four men with rifles surround a cart with a great square chest, wolves in the snow, the low red sun. Their faces are not seen.

Shot: wide. A young woman in a dark cloak running down the snowy slope from a great rock toward the stone bridge at sunset, her cloak flying, below her on the bridge men kneeling around a fallen man beside an empty broken box, the gypsies riding away over the far end of the bridge, the castle against the red sky. Her face is not seen.
